messages:
olivia: FYI seeing a weird pattern this morning — multiple GPU-capable pods pending but CPU nodes are picking up similar workloads. GPU node pool shows ~0 pods, but pending queue has ~12 pods with nodeSelectors for gpu=true. cc @sam @chen

sam: screenshots/logs? is this a taint/toleration mismatch or CA not scaling the GPU nodegroup?

olivia: pasting the pod spec from one of the pending jobs (sanitized):

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: tensor-infer-abc
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: gpu
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-pool"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "dedicated"
    effect: "NoExecute"
```

olivia: our GPU taint is `gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule` (checked on node). Looks like the toleration key and effect are both wrong (and value mismatch). pods tolerate NoExecute but taint is NoSchedule + key different. oops.

chen: also noticed some GPU nodes in the us-west-2-gpu-asg were stuck in NotReady intermittently earlier — autoscaler-bot shows scale-up but node never joined the cluster for ~10m due to egress/NAT error. CA may have given up before useful capacity came up.

autoscaler-bot: [event] cluster-autoscaler triggered scale-up for nodegroup us-west-2-gpu-asg -> desired=4 (reason: 12 unschedulable pods). New instances launched at 2025-03-12T08:41:12Z. Some instances failed to register within 300s.

sam: two separate failures then: pod tolerations wrong so pods won't schedule even if node exists + CA's node registration failure window causing delayed capacity. we should fix toleration in the deployment template asap.

maria: quick patch to add correct toleration + nodeAffinity suggestion:

```
kubectl patch deploy tensor-infer -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu","operator":"Equal","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```

maria: and add nodeAffinity to prefer nodes with label accelerator=gpu so we don't rely on tolerations alone.

jon: For the CA/egress issue I dug into the usw2 subnet changes — the new GPU pool ended up in a subnet without a NAT gateway due to a Terraform merge conflict. Instances launched but kubelet couldn't talk to our control plane or S3 during bootstrap, so they never registered. I opened a quick infra PR to reattach NAT for the GPU subnet.

olivia: thanks — will patch the deployment now. Also can we add a lint rule to our CI to disallow tolerations referencing keys other than 'gpu' or 'node.kubernetes.io/*'? This class of typo keeps cropping up.

sam: +1. we should also add a small e2e in staging that launches a tiny GPU pod and verifies scheduling to a GPU nodegroup (and CA creates one if empty). catches both toleration & CA gaps.

maria: we might also consider setting the GPU nodegroup to 'initialMin=1' for critical clusters to avoid warm-up delay and NAT misconfigs causing total capacity loss. cost trade-off but saves us from outages during onboarding.

jon: agree on initialMin but prefer a less costly option first: set the GPU nodepool to use cheap spot instances for a baseline 1 and autoscale to on-demand for higher demand. saves $$$ and keeps at least 1 node ready.

olivia: patch applied, pods are now scheduling (6/12 started). Opening a short postmortem with action items: fix TF subnet PR, add CI lint for toleration keys, add staging e2e, and evaluate initialMin/spot baseline.

sam: nice. can you add the PR links and assign owners? i'll take the CI lint.

olivia: will do — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
